CONTEXT: Planning a build of **SFCC-91 — "PDP UI — Colour Swatches & Variation Selection"** as if from scratch. There is an existing branch and PR for this story by another developer — **ignore both entirely**; we are planning a fresh build. Work only from `develop` (HEAD 269d5d4).

Report:

**1. WHAT ALREADY EXISTS ON `develop`.** Is there any colour-swatch or variation-selection code already merged? Check:
   - `overrides/app/components/swatch-group/` — does it exist as an override, or is it still base-only in `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/swatch-group/`?
   - `overrides/app/components/product-view/` — what does it currently render for variation selection?
   - `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/` — the PDP page and its partials
   - `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms|molecules|organisms/` — full current inventory, since a new component would land here

**2. THE NEAREST EXISTING PATTERN.** This codebase has strong precedent. For a new PDP component, what is the established shape? Look at the most recently added ui-kit components (the `zimmProduct*` family from SFCC-89, and `zimmProductPrice` from SFCC-194) and report: folder layout, `index.tsx` shape, co-located `<name>.css.ts` recipe shape, registration in `theme/components/index.ts`, story, test. Give me the actual file list of one exemplar so a builder can mirror it.

**3. TIERS AND OWNERSHIP.** For every file a colour-swatch/variation-selection story would plausibly touch, give the protection tier and owner from `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md` and `.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md` — NOT from `.claude/registry/*.md`, whose Tier column is a derived heuristic and wrong in places. Flag any Tier 1 file. Note that `overrides/app/components/swatch-group/` is listed in protectedFiles.md — confirm and give its owner.

**4. BLAST RADIUS.** For each likely-touched existing file, how many other files import it? Use a grep across `overrides/app` excluding `.test.` and `.stories.`. Flag anything above 5 consumers.

**5. THE OVERRIDE-VS-CUSTOM CALL.** For each piece of this story, does a base file exist at the mirrored path under `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/`? Answer concretely per file. Where a base exists, note whether SFCC's own components import it (grep `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/` for it) — that determines whether the default export must stay a faithful port.

**6. THE EXEMPLAR PRs.** Read PR #59 (footer, the component+CSS layer) and PR #56 (the token layer) via `gh pr view` and `gh pr diff --name-only`. Report what pattern each establishes that this story must follow.

**7. STATE OF THE STYLING RULE.** Read `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` and report the CURRENT direction of the `var(--zimm-*)` rule — does it belong in the recipe or in component JSX? Quote the exact lines. This rule has reversed direction before, so quote rather than summarise.

Cite `file:line` throughout. Distinguish what you VERIFIED by reading or running from what you inferred. End with a section headed exactly `What I could not verify`.

=== overrideStyling.md lines 1-45 ===
# Styling an Override Component

How to style a component under `overrides/app/components/` or `overrides/app/theme/`.
Cross-references [overrides.md](./overrides.md) (module-replacement correctness — a
different concern: that file is about not breaking SFCC's own imports, this one is
about what values to reach for once the component compiles). Day-to-day CSS/token
rules live in [css.md](./css.md); this file is the practical "what do I actually type"
companion.

---

## The hierarchy — reach for these in order

1. **`textStyle` prop** for anything textual. `textStyle="body2"`, never a raw `fontSize`.
   All 22 Handover text styles are registered in `theme/foundation/typography.ts`.
2. **Raw `var(--zimm-*)` CSS custom properties** for colour and spacing — `color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)"`,
   `bg="var(--zimm-color-bg-02)"`, `gap="var(--zimm-scale-m)"`. **Never** a bare Chakra/theme
   token string (`color="text.default"`, `gap="m"`) — even though `theme.colors`/`theme.space`
   ARE registered from the same Zimmermann foundations (see `theme/index.ts`'s own comment on
   which scales are and aren't registered) and a bare key resolves to the identical value. This
   is a house-style requirement, not a correctness one: a `var(--zimm-*)` reference is
   unambiguous at every call site, where a bare key forces a PR reviewer to check
   `theme/index.ts`'s registered-scale list to know whether it happens to be correct. Mechanically
   enforced across every recipe file by `theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts`'s "no
   override-component style uses a bare token key on a registered scale" test — it walks the
   registered recipe map only, so it cannot see the same mistake made as a JSX/`sx` prop (see
   that test's SCOPE note); apply the same discipline there by hand.
3. **A component's own theme config** — either centralized (`theme/components/<name>.ts`)
   or, per the co-location pattern below, beside the component as `<name>.css.ts` — for
   anything that needs to vary by variant/size/state and isn't already a Chakra prop — see
   "Component-local tokens" and "Co-locating a component's theme file" below. For an
   interactive component with existing Chakra support (buttons, inputs, etc.), this theme
   config is the single source of truth — see "One canonical styling surface per component
   type" below.
4. **`sx` prop** for a one-off Chakra-prop-system gap, per [css.md](./css.md).
5. **Scoped `.scss`** only when `sx` genuinely can't express it (complex pseudo-selectors,
   keyframes) — same file, same rules as [css.md](./css.md) already documents.

**Never**: a raw hex/px/rem/em literal in a component file — reach for the token
instead. The one standing exception is `zimmButton.css.ts`'s provisional height/padding

When a component needs a spacing/sizing value that already has a `spacing.ts` /
`iconSizes` / etc. entry, reference that entry **as a `var(--zimm-*)` custom property**
— `marginBottom: 'var(--zimm-scale-xs)'`, not `marginBottom: 2`, not
`marginBottom: '0.5rem'`, and **not** the bare key `marginBottom: 'xs'`. The bare-key
form resolved correctly against the registered `theme.space` and was what this section
used to recommend, but hierarchy point 2 above now forbids it and
`theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts`'s bare-token guard **fails the build on it** —
so following the old advice inside a registered recipe breaks `npm run test`.

See `overrides/app/components/footer/footer.css.ts` and
`.../footer/bottomBar/bottomBar.css.ts` for the pattern in a real recipe. The reason is
traceability, not parity with the base theme: a `var(--zimm-*)` reference names the
Figma token it came from, where a raw `2` or `'0.5rem'` names nothing. (Note these
recipes are deliberately namespaced `ZimmFooter*` so they do **not** inherit the base
SFCC `Footer` config — their values come from Figma, not from re-expressing base
numerics. See `recipeGuards.test.ts`'s namespacing guard.)

**Responsive steps are explicit media queries, not Chakra's array shorthand.** A
co-located recipe keys them off `BP` in `theme/components/footerShared.ts`, in the form:

```ts
[`@media (min-width: ${BP.tablet})`]: { gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-3xl)' },
```

`footer.css.ts`'s `contentRow` and `linksInner` parts are the reference.

feat(product-view): add renderHeader slot for caller-supplied header content

Adds one optional prop to ProductView so a caller can supply the header block, and
corrects two documentation claims in the same file that were false or misleading.

The slot
---------
renderHeader?: (props: ProductViewHeaderProps) => React.ReactNode

Its default renders the same private ProductViewHeader the base file renders inline, with
the identical six values, so omitting it is behaviour-preserving. Both header call sites
route through it — base renders the header twice behind responsive display arrays, and a
slot only one of them honoured would be a silent half-override.

Prop, default and call sites are one atomic unit, not three separable edits: deleting the
default alone produces TS2722 at both call sites.

----------------------------------------------------------
overrideStyling.md prescribes putting Zimmermann-only additions behind a named export that
wraps the default. That route cannot express this requirement: a wrapper can only set props
the default already accepts, so letting a caller replace an internal render block still
requires the slot on the default. The only alternative is forking the component body, which
is a graver breach of the faithful-port rule.

The rule's stated purpose is served. renderHeader has zero occurrences in the base package,
and the four base modules that import product-view — product-view-modal/index.jsx,
product-view-modal/bundle.jsx, bonus-product-view-modal/index.jsx and
pages/product-detail/index.jsx — neither pass it nor are affected by it. forwardRef
behaviour is unchanged.

either centralized as `theme/components/<name>.ts` or, per the co-location pattern below,
beside the component as `<name>.css.ts` — consumed via Chakra's component (`<Button>`,
`<Link>` variant, etc.). Don't also give it a `.zimm-*` global class in
`globalStyles.ts` — a static CSS class can't express `_hover`/`_active`/`_disabled`/
`_focusVisible` states the way a Chakra theme config can, so a class "mirror" is
structurally incomplete from the start, and nothing stops its values from disagreeing
with the real theme config over time. `zimmButton.css.ts` (co-located at `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton/`) is the single source of truth for
button styling; `globalStyles.ts` has no `.zimm-btn-*` classes — use Chakra's `<Button>`
for any button, not a class.

`.zimm-*` classes remain the right tool for genuinely static, non-interactive,
massively-reused treatments (typography, the responsive grid, form-field layout) where
there's no interactive state to lose.

### Recipe or JSX? The rule text and the code disagree — read this carefully

The **rule text is agnostic on location**: hierarchy point 2's examples are written as **JSX props** (`color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)"`, `gap="var(--zimm-scale-m)"`), so on a literal reading `var(--zimm-*)` is permitted in JSX. Point 2 forbids the *bare key*, not the *JSX location*.

But the surrounding rules push everything into the recipe. `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`, "One canonical styling surface per component type", verbatim:

> ```
> Only one place should define how a given interactive component looks: its theme config —
> either centralized as `theme/components/<name>.ts` or, per the co-location pattern below,
> beside the component as `<name>.css.ts` — consumed via Chakra's component (`<Button>`,
> `<Link>` variant, etc.).
> ```

**The de-facto convention in code is overwhelmingly "recipe", and it is near-absolute.** Verified by grep across `overrides/app/components`:
- **17 `.css.ts` recipe files** contain `var(--zimm-*)`
- **exactly 1 component `.tsx`** contains it (excluding stories/tests): `overrides/app/components/footer/footerNavColumn/index.tsx:44` and `:62` — and both are inside a `__css={{ ...styles.part, ...conditional }}` spread, i.e. a conditional the recipe genuinely cannot express, not ordinary styling.

Every `zimmProduct*` component applies styling **only** via `__css={styles.part}` with zero inline token values. So: **put `var(--zimm-*)` in the co-located `<name>.css.ts` recipe.** Reach for a JSX `__css` spread only for a genuinely conditional value, following `footerNavColumn`'s shape.

One caveat the rule states explicitly: the guard *"walks the registered recipe map only, so it cannot see the same mistake made as a JSX/`sx` prop… apply the same discipline there by hand."* The JSX half is unenforced. Note also `textStyle` stays a bare key — `.claude/rules/css.md` says there is no `var(--zimm-*)` substitute for the composite expansion.
